claude.country: Multi-institutional (five institutions; country not stated in text)

links.outcome: Repeatability of LLM outputs across repeated runs, and effect of prompt (simple vs optimised)
links.effect: Repeatability varied widely from 12.7% (Med-LMop) to 39.0% (GPT-4sp); optimised prompts improved accuracy, e.g. Med-LM lesion-level LI-RADS accuracy 40.8% (sp) vs 61.3% (op).

links.outcome: Comparison of GPT-4 vs medically fine-tuned Med-LM on same CT reports against radiologist LI-RADS reference
links.effect: Med-LMop had the highest performance in all analyses and was statistically superior to other models (all p < 0.001); lesion-level LI-RADS accuracy 40.8%-61.3%.
links.quote: Med-LMop demonstrated the highest performance in all analyses and was statistically superior to other models (all p < 0.001).

unlisted_practices: Prompt optimisation to improve LLM classification accuracy
Medical fine-tuning of LLM versus general-purpose LLM

links.quote: Lesion- and patient-level accuracies for LI-RADS scoring ranged from 40.8% (Med-LMsp) to 61.3% (Med-LMop) and from 27.7% (Med-LMsp) to 52.4% (Med-LMop), respectively.

links.effect: Lesion-information Likert scores differed significantly between correctly and incorrectly classified lesions (all p ≤ 0.04).
links.quote: Kappa values were weak to moderate between the two reviewers in different aspects of report quality (0.471-0.766), and Likert scores for lesion information differed significantly between correctly and incorrectly classified lesions (all p ≤ 0.04).
